rfi.title: South Africa unrest grows as migrants become ‘scapegoats’
rfi.description: South Africa is once again facing a rise in anti-migrant tensions, with vigilante groups reportedly going door to door demanding that undocumented foreign nationals leave the country by the end of June. Post-apartheid specialist Cécile Perrot tells RFI the violence reflects deeper social and economic problems and that migrants have increasingly become scapegoats for poverty and unemployment.

rfi.title: France questions judicial system after girl's suspected murder
rfi.description: France's government was on Friday assessing possible judicial failings, after allegations that investigators could have prevented a 11-year-old girl's disappearance by better dealing with previous sexual abuse complaints.

rfi.title: Dozens dead of thirst after truck breaks down in Niger desert
rfi.description: Forty-nine people died of dehydration in a remote part of the Sahara desert in north-west Niger after the truck transporting them broke down, authorities said on Thursday.

rfi.title: French billionaire Stérin reveals far-right agenda in first public hearing
rfi.description: French billionaire Pierre-Edouard Stérin has used his first appearance before lawmakers to lay bare his "meta-political" campaign to bring free-market and conservative ideas into power to battle "socialism, wokism, Islamism and immigration", less than a year before France’s presidential election.

rfi.description: France's parliament has overwhelmingly approved a bill to curb exposure to cadmium, a toxic heavy metal found in phosphate fertilisers, setting up a political clash with the government and raising fresh questions about France's links to Moroccan phosphate imports.

rfi.title: Chwalinska beats Shnaider to set up Andreeva clash in French Open women's final
rfi.description: Maja Chwalinska beat the 25th seed Diana Shnaider on Thursday to make history as the first qualifier to reach the French Open final since tennis was opened up to professional players in 1968.

rfi.description: Franco-Iranian author and film director Marjane Satrapi, best known for the graphic novel and film Persepolis, has died aged 56.

rfi.title: French start-up Quobly raises €115m to build cheaper quantum computers
rfi.description: French start-up Quobly secured €115 million in funding this week as it pursues an ambitious goal: building quantum computers using the same manufacturing techniques as ordinary computer chips.

rfi.title: Podcast: Protecting whistleblowers, homegrown fertiliser, daylight savings in France
rfi.description: A former prime minister goes after a whistleblower and what that means for those who dare to speak out. Why a natural ingredient that could cover up to 40 percent of France's fertiliser needs is currently being flushed down the loo. And France's halting steps towards adopting daylight savings time.

rfi.title: Israel strikes Lebanon after truce announcement
rfi.description: Israel struck south Lebanon on Thursday and threatened new attacks on Beirut despite an announcement hours earlier that Israel and Lebanon had agreed to implement a conditional ceasefire.

rfi.title: France recognises role in pesticide harm across Caribbean islands
rfi.description: France's parliament has unanimously acknowledged the state's role in a pesticide scandal that contaminated most people in Guadeloupe and Martinique and has been linked to cancer and other health problems. The vote marks a significant moment in a decades-long fight over chlordecone, a toxic chemical that continued to be used in the French Caribbean after it was banned in mainland France.

rfi.title: France and Rwanda unite to honour genocide victims with Paris monument
rfi.description: Rwanda's President Paul Kagame visited Paris on Tuesday to unveil a monument dedicated to victims of the Rwandan genocide, alongside French President Emmanuel Macron, in a further acknowledgement by France of its role in one of the worst atrocities of the 20th century.

rfi.title: EU unveils plan to cut dependence on US and Asian technology
rfi.description: Europe is launching a sweeping push to reduce its dependence on American and Asian technology, with plans to boost homegrown chips, cloud computing and artificial intelligence while keeping greater control over data and key digital services.

rfi.title: Tanzania's Hassan makes historic Russia visit amid frayed ties with West
rfi.description: Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan begins a three-day state visit to Russia on Wednesday – the first official trip by a Tanzanian head of state to Moscow since 1969 – as her government faces growing criticism from Western countries over violence linked to the country's 2025 elections.

euronews.description: Hundreds of worshippers gathered in Bavaria on 4 June for Seehausen's traditional Corpus Christi lake procession. The event, held annually since 1935, combines religious devotion with local heritage on the waters of Staffelsee.

lemonde.title: Les Chinois rechignent à consommer, un problème pour l’économie mondiale
lemonde.description: La crise du secteur immobilier des années 2020, qui a englouti une bonne part de leurs économies, la surproduction industrielle qui freine les salaires et le faible niveau de couverture sociale se traduisent par une plus grande prudence dans les dépenses.

france24fr.title: Mondial de foot selon Donald Trump : vous n'êtes pas les bienvenus
france24fr.description: À quelques jours du coup d'envoi de la Coupe du monde de football en Amérique du Nord, rarement le climat aura été aussi hostile envers les spectateurs étrangers. france24fr.title: Un village opte pour le tout-solaire face à la montée des factures de l'énergie
france24fr.description: Une électricité verte, 30 % moins chère et sans impôts supplémentaires : c'est possible, grâce au solaire. Dès 2011, la commune d'Escourse (dans les Landes) a investi 1,2 million d'euros dans le solaire. Et aujourd'hui, ça paie. Particuliers, mais aussi commerces, associations et éclairage public sont alimentés grâce aux panneaux. La commune est à présent autonome à 60 % en électricité. Reportage de nos confrères de France 2.

Fuite d'air à bord de l'ISS : les astronautes peuvent finalement regagner la station
france24fr.description: Après avoir reçu, vendredi, l'ordre de la Nasa de se préparer à une éventuelle évacuation en raison de l'aggravation d'une fuite d'air à bord, les astronautes de la Station spatiale internationale vont finalement pouvoir regagner l'intérieur de l'ISS, a déclaré un porte-parole de la Nasa à l'AFP.

france24fr.title: Flottille pour Gaza : une enquête ouverte à Paris pour "tortures" et "crime de guerre"
Nouvelle-Calédonie : l'île des Pins espère reconquérir ses touristes
france24fr.description: Depuis la crise du Covid-19 et les émeutes de mai 2024, l'économie calédonienne est en souffrance, notamment le secteur du tourisme. C'est le cas à l'île des Pins, où tout est mis en œuvre pour reconquérir les clients.

france24fr.title: Flottille pour Gaza : une enquête ouverte à Paris pour "tortures" et "crime de guerre"
france24fr.description: Le parquet national antiterroriste français a ouvert une enquête pour "tortures" et "crime de guerre", à la suite d'un signalement du gouvernement sur la manière dont des Français de la flottille pour Gaza ont été traités par les autorités israéliennes.

france24fr.title: Japon : traque d'un ours "extrêmement intelligent", les autorités appellent à la prudence
france24fr.description: Les autorités japonaises traquent vendredi un ours décrit comme "extrêmement intelligent" ayant blessé quatre personnes dans le nord, soupçonné d'avoir déverrouillé une fenêtre et ouvert un robinet dans sa fuite.

france24fr.title: Explosion d'un drone ukrainien en Roumanie : le brouillage électronique russe pointé du doigt
france24fr.description: Une semaine après l'explosion d'un drone russe sur un immeuble à Galati, la Roumanie a de nouveau fait les frais de l'explosion d'un drone – cette fois, maritime et ukrainien – dans le port de Constanta, sur la mer Noire. Aucune victime n'est à déplorer. L'Ukraine a admis que le drone lui appartenait, et a précisé qu'il avait été "perturbé" par le brouillage électronique russe.

france24fr.title: Disparition de Lyhanna : le drame dans le sud ouest prend une tournure politique
france24fr.description: Au lendemain de la découverte dans le Gers d'un corps étant probablement celui de Lyhanna, 11 ans, l'exécutif a déploré vendredi des dysfonctionnements "accablants”. Le procureur d'Agen devrait dévoiler en fin de journée les résultats de l'autopsie.

france24fr.title: En Inde, la Gen Z et le "parti des cafards" se prépare à manifester
france24fr.description: En Inde, le fondateur du nouveau parti, dit du "peuple des cafards", créé récemment en réaction aux propos méprisants d'un magistrat envers la jeunesse, doit arriver aujourd'hui dans la capitale New Delhi pour une manifestation. Son parti se moque de la formation nationaliste hindoue, le BJP du Premier ministre Narendra Modi.

france24fr.title: Sanctions économiques des Etats-Unis à Cuba : les entreprises étrangères quittent le pays
france24fr.description: Le gouvernement de Donald Trump a accentué jeudi sa pression sur Cuba en plaçant sous sanctions économiques plusieurs personnalités du pays, dont le président Miguel Diaz-Canel et des membres de la famille Castro. Plusieurs entreprises étrangères ont réduit, voire mis fin à leurs activités à Cuba sous la pression des Etats-Unis et face au risque d'être exposées à des sanctions en raison de leurs liens avec le conglomérat économico-militaire cubain Gaesa.

france24fr.title: En RD Congo, plusieurs généraux de l'armée devant la justice
france24fr.description: 🇨🇩 En République démocratique du Congo s’est ouvert ce jeudi 4 juin 2026 le procès de plusieurs généraux de l’armée. Sur le banc des accusés, l’ex-chef d’état-major, le général Christian Tshiwewe Songesa, ainsi que John Numbi, ancien inspecteur général des FARDC actuellement en fuite. Tous sont poursuivis devant la Haute Cour militaire pour de lourdes charges.

france24fr.title: Côte d’Ivoire, une souche virale menace les récoltes de manioc
france24fr.description:
La Côte d’Ivoire est en état d’alerte après la découverte d’une souche virale très agressive, originaire d’Ouganda, dans des plantations de manioc de l’ouest du pays.
 
Cette menace fait craindre une importante baisse de la production nationale. 
 
Les autorités rassurent et mettent en place des mesures pour éviter la propagation du virus.

france24fr.title: Alerte sur le manioc : une souche virale détectée dans les plantations de Côte d'Ivoire
france24fr.description: Une souche virale d’origine ougandaise, particulièrement agressive, a été confirmée dans des plantations de manioc de l’ouest de la Côte d’Ivoire. Une menace qui fait déjà craindre une forte baisse de la production nationale et qui mobilise autorités et professionnels de la filière.

france24fr.title: Lunettes connectées : ce "second cerveau" qui veut vous aider au quotidien
france24fr.description: Connaissez-vous Mira ? Comme Google, Samsung, Xreal, Engo et Meta, cette entreprise créée par deux anciens de Harvard a mis au point des lunettes connectées permettant, entre autre, de retrouver son chemin ou ses clés, écouter de la musique ou encore traduire. Mais entre assistants cognitifs, risques de menace sur la vie privée et nouveaux outils professionnels, ces "seconds cerveaux" modifient notre rapport à la réalité.

france24fr.title: Insécurité sur le corridor Guinée-Mali : une économie au ralenti et des familles inquiètes
france24fr.description: Sur le corridor Guinée-Mali, le transport routier est fortement perturbé. Depuis les attaques survenues fin avril, la situation sécuritaire s’est nettement dégradée sur cet axe stratégique reliant les deux pays. La circulation des personnes et des marchandises est fortement perturbée. Conséquences : une économie qui tourne au ralenti et des familles sans nouvelles de leurs proches partis sur les routes. Reportage de Sarah Sakho et Malick Diakité.

france24fr.title: Attaques xénophobes en Afrique du Sud : plus de 500 migrants accueillis dans des centres
france24fr.description: Les tensions autour de la présence d’étrangers en situation irrégulière continuent d’alimenter des violences dans certaines régions d’Afrique du Sud. Le Mozambique affirme qu’au moins cinq de ses ressortissants ont été tués dans ce qu’il qualifie d’attaques xénophobes liées aux troubles survenus dans la ville côtière de Mossel Bay.

observador.description: Quatro astronautas da missão Crew-12 ficaram abrigados dentro da nave da SpaceX "por precaução". Roscosmos agendou trabalhos de reparação mais abrangentes no módulo Zvezda esta sexta-feira.

observador.description: Presidente da Federação Portuguesa de Concessionários de Praia afirmou que indefinição da legislação da APA cria dificuldades e não acompanha a realidade das praias, mas garantiu o cumprimento da lei.

observador.description: A rutura do medicamento para a prevenção de doenças cardiovasculares está relacionada com dificuldades de produção que não são especificadas. Ainda, o preço do gasóleo deve subir na próxima semana.

observador.title: MAI anuncia reforço de 340 operacionais nos aeroportos
observador.description: Luis Neves anunciou que reforço nos aeroportos começa no próximo dia 4, com 340 elementos de segurança, mas relembrou que "até chegar ao ponto ótimo", "há questões digitais que têm de ser resolvidas".

observador.title: Ainda não parece mas o Mundial está aí à porta
observador.description: Mundial com mais equipas, mais jogadores, mais jogos, mais países e mais estádios arranca na quinta-feira, dia em que Portugal ainda prepara a viagem para os EUA após particulares com Chile e Nigéria.

observador.title: Montenegro espera que integração dos Balcãs tenha sucesso
observador.description: Luís Montenegro diz ser "consequência feliz" que se esteja a discutir o alargamento do bloco aos Balcãs, nos 40 anos de adesão portuguesa, desejando que a cimeira reforce a conectividade entre países.

observador.title: Moscovo e Kiev trocam 370 prisioneiros de guerra
observador.description: Rússia e Ucrânia trocaram respetivamente 185 prisioneiros de guerra esta sexta-feira. EAU desempenharam papel de mediação numa das poucas áreas de cooperação entre os dois países.

observador.title: MAI orgulhoso do trabalho da PSP no dia da greve geral
observador.description: Luís Neves destacou o apoio ao trabalho realizado pela PSP, na quarta-feira: "Tenho orgulho no trabalho que fizeram, não pode haver nem desordem, nem desacatos", afirmou o ministro.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Uno-Sicherheitsrat, Boeing 787, Nastassja Kinski und Wim Wenders
spiegel.description: Am größten deutschen Flughafen untersuchen Experten die Lufthansa-Maschine, deren Fahrwerk plötzlich wegklappte. Deutschland bewirbt sich erneut um einen Sitz im Uno-Sicherheitsrat. Und Nastassja Kinski äußert sich zur Debatte über die Nacktszene im Wenders-Film. Das ist die Lage am Freitagabend.

spiegel.title: Friedich Merz kündigt erneute Kandidatur für Uno-Sicherheitsrat für 2035/36
spiegel.description: Nach der krachenden Niederlage im Uno-Sicherheitsrat hat sich der Kanzler zu Wort gemeldet. Deutschland wird 2035/36 erneut für einen Sitz im Gremium kandidieren.

spiegel.title: Russland: AfD-Delegation bei Putins Wirtschaftsforum in Sankt Petersburg
spiegel.description: AfD-Politiker reisen zu Putins Wirtschaftsforum nach Sankt Petersburg. Was die Rechtsextremen dort über Deutschland erzählen, klingt unheilvoll. Ebenso wie das, was Putin über die AfD sagt.

spiegel.title: USA: US-Senat billigt 70 Milliarden Dollar für Anti-Migrationspolitik
spiegel.description: Die Republikaner haben sich im Senat gegen die Demokraten durchgesetzt und 70 Milliarden Dollar freigegeben, die auch an die US-Einwanderungsbehörde ICE fließen sollen. Sie steht wegen ihres brutalen Vorgehens in der Kritik.

spiegel.title: Hunter Biden hat als »Crack-Junkie« viel zu sagen
spiegel.description: Lange wurde in der Familie Biden über Hunters Drogenkonsum geschwiegen. Zum Jubiläum seiner Abstinenz legt er nun auf Social Media los und scherzt über seine Sucht – und seine Kritiker.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Europäer planen Treffen mit Selenskyj nach Angebot an Putin
spiegel.description: Selenskyj hat Putin direkte Gespräche angeboten. Darüber wollen die Europäer am Sonntag mit dem ukrainischen Präsidenten sprechen. Die Bundesregierung unterstützt dessen Vorstoß.

spiegel.title: »Nius«: BVG stoppt Werbung für Julian Reichelts Portal
spiegel.description: Das rechte Krawallmedium von Ex-»Bild«-Chefredakteur Julian Reichelt sorgte mit einer Kampagne im Berliner Nahverkehr für Proteste. Nun hat die BVG die Werbung gestoppt, wegen eines neuen Motivs.

spiegel.title: Krefeld: Ausgebüxter Serval im Krefelder Zoo wieder aufgetaucht
spiegel.description: Im Krefelder Zoo wurde eine Wildkatze vermisst. Polizei und Zoo suchten nach dem Tier. Nun ist es wieder aufgetaucht – nicht weit entfernt.

spiegel.title: ICE will Todesfälle von kürzlich freigelassenen Menschen offenbar nicht mehr melden
spiegel.description: Bereits 18 Menschen sind in diesem Jahr in ICE-Gewahrsam gestorben. Jetzt will die Behörde einem Bericht der »Washington Post« zufolge eine etablierte Praxis aus Biden-Zeiten einstellen.

spiegel.title: A20 in Niedersachsen: Start der Bauarbeiten für umstrittene Moorautobahn
spiegel.description: Trotz des Sanierungsstaus bei alten Autobahnen, baut Deutschland sogar neue Trassen. Der Verkehrsminister hat gleich zwei Großbaustellen im Norden eröffnet. Jetzt wird auch kostbarer Moorboden asphaltiert.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Kai Wegner mit eigenem Truck beim CSD in Berlin
spiegel.description: Im vergangenen Jahr hatte sich die CDU auf vielen Pride-Paraden rar gemacht. Dieses Jahr nimmt Berlins Regierender Bürgermeister Kai Wegner prominent am CSD der Hauptstadt teil – mit eigens designtem Vehikel.

spiegel.title: ISS: Luftleck im russischen Segment versetzt Raumstation in Alarmzustand
spiegel.description: Wegen eines Luftlecks im russischen Segment der Internationalen Raumstation hat die Nasa die Crew angewiesen, sich in ihre Raumkapseln zurückzuziehen. Möglicherweise muss bald evakuiert werden.

spiegel.title: Rumänien: Seedrohne explodiert vor Hafenstadt Konstanza
spiegel.description: In der rumänischen Hafenstadt Konstanza ist am Morgen eine Drohne explodiert. Laut Kyjiw kam sie aus der Ukraine. Es ist das zweite Mal innerhalb kurzer Zeit, dass Russlands Angriffskrieg gegen die Ukraine das EU-Land erreicht.

spiegel.title: »Area 51«: Mysteriöser Jet wohl über geheimer US-Militärbasis gesichtet
spiegel.description: Ein unbekanntes Flugobjekt soll nahe der sagenumwobenen Luftwaffenbasis »Area 51« in Nevada aufgetaucht sein. Mindestens zwei Erklärungen klingen plausibel.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: »Mehrzweckeier« wird zum neuesten Protest gegen den Kanzler
spiegel.description: »Lackaffe«, »Lügen-Fritze«, »Merz leck Eier«: Der Kanzler muss sich im Netz viel Spott gefallen lassen. Nun könnte eine Varianz der Schmähungen gar Jugendwort des Jahres werden. Und die CDU beginnt, sich locker zu machen.

spiegel.title: Türkei-Podcast: Droht Recep Tayyip Erdoğan das gleiche Schicksal wie Viktor Orbán?
spiegel.description: Ein türkisches Gericht hat Özgür Özel als Oppositionschef abgesetzt – er wurde Präsident Erdoğan wohl zu gefährlich. Doch das Manöver des Langzeitherrschers könnte sich rächen.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Stahlunternehmen beklagen Produktionsausfälle durch Schienenchaos
spiegel.description: Unternehmen warnen wegen der Probleme bei der Bahn vor negativen Folgen für den Standort Deutschland. Ein Stahlhersteller hat die Produktion offenbar bereits zurückgefahren – wegen des Baustellenchaos in Norddeutschland.

spiegel.description: Moskau und Kyjiw haben je 185 Gefangene ausgetauscht. Unter ihnen soll auch ein Zivilist sein – und Menschen, die seit 2022 in Gefangenschaft waren. Die Vereinigten Arabischen Emirate sollen vermittelt haben.

phys-org.title: White storks: Why introducing non‑native species in rewilding projects can be a good idea
phys-org.description: White storks (Ciconia ciconia) are a majestic bird with a two-meter wingspan and an enormous circular nest.

phys-org.title: Hawai'i's last false killer whales threatened by nutritional stress and warming seas
phys-org.description: A seven-year collaborative study has revealed alarming fluctuations in the health of Hawaii's endangered insular false killer whales, with some individuals losing nearly a quarter of their body weight in just a few months. Published in Endangered Species Research, the findings provide the first quantitative evidence that nutritional stress and environmental shifts may be driving the decline of this iconic population, which now numbers fewer than 140 individuals.

phys-org.title: India gained 2.1 million hectares of dry woodland in a decade, major study finds
phys-org.description: India gained around 2.1 million hectares of tropical dry woodland between 2014 and 2024—an area larger than Wales—according to a major new study involving researchers from The University of Manchester's Global Development Institute. The research was published in the journal Environmental Research Letters.

phys-org.title: Deep-sea supergiant isopods last years without food by using a two-part survival system
phys-org.description: The supergiant bathynomid is a deep-sea isopod famous for surviving more than five years without food. Despite residing in an extremely low-nutrient habitat, these organisms exhibit pronounced body gigantism, a trait that requires substantial energy. This raises an energy paradox: How do these apparently energy-hungry isopods sustain their enormous size given the sporadic availability of food in the deep sea?

phys-org.title: How the body creates reliable antibodies out of biological chaos
phys-org.description: A new study tracking thousands of B cells across more than 100 germinal centers in mice reveals how the system consistently produces highly effective antibodies. The findings overturn longstanding ideas about how germinal centers function, revealing that they are far more selective than once thought, and challenges the idea that antibody improvement is driven mainly by rare growth "bursts" among the most successful B cells.

phys-org.title: Ocean conservation needs strong relationships, not just targets
phys-org.description: With World Oceans Day coming up on June 8, policymakers and researchers will be thinking about the state of the ocean and efforts to protect marine environments.

phys-org.title: Wildfires are reversing America's progress on ozone pollution
phys-org.description: For decades, the United States made steady progress in reducing surface ozone pollution, the main ingredient in smog. But that progress—made as vehicles, industries, and power sources became cleaner—is increasingly being overshadowed by a different and growing source of ozone pollution: wildfires.

phys-org.title: Invasive caiman may pose new challenges for Everglades restoration
phys-org.description: In the canals, wetlands and marshes of the Florida Everglades, the spectacled caiman has quietly expanded its foothold, threatening an already-vulnerable ecosystem. A new University of Florida study published in Frontiers in Amphibian and Reptile Science synthesizes more than 70 years of research on the invasive species native to Central and South America that has firmly established itself across the most vulnerable part of the Sunshine State—the Florida Everglades.

phys-org.title: Study shows indoor air contains greater diversity of airborne fungi than previously thought
phys-org.description: Researchers from Imperial College London have conducted the U.K.'s largest-ever longitudinal study of indoor fungal air pollution, revealing that homes are active fungal ecosystems rather than passive recipients of outdoor air. The West London Healthy Home and Environment Study (WellHome), led by researchers from Imperial's School of Public Health, analyzed the air in 118 households over a two-year period. The study focuses on children with asthma or allergies and families from ethnic

phys-org.title: How an app is growing social connections for people with disability and caregivers
phys-org.description: Almost 1 in 3 Australians experiences loneliness. For people with disability and care workers, that number can be even greater.

phys-org.title: With ShakeAlert installations complete, researchers explore offshore expansion
phys-org.description: The ShakeAlert earthquake early warning system has been rapidly expanding since its launch in 2021. Now, researchers at University of Washington affiliated Pacific Northwest Seismic Network (PNSN) have finished all planned installations, bringing the two-state total to 569 seismic monitoring stations spread across Washington and Oregon.

phys-org.title: Prescribed burns are lit in Australia's Northern Territory to minimize the severity of fires later in the season
phys-org.description: In May and June of most years, NASA satellites typically begin to detect large numbers of wildland fires throughout the Top End and Arnhem Land regions of Australia's Northern Territory. On some days, especially in the afternoon, the blazes can resemble sizable wildfires in satellite imagery, spreading widely and producing expansive smoke plumes.

phys-org.title: From forest to front door: Understanding how wildfire spreads through communities
phys-org.description: As California's population boomed—from 10 million in 1950 to over 40 million today—the number of people living in fire-prone areas multiplied. Over the decades, millions of new homes and commercial buildings sprang up to accommodate the needs of the state's growing population, and many of those structures stand in areas prone to wildfires.

phys-org.title: Hidden meltwater found deep in Antarctic coastal waters reveals stronger climate impacts
phys-org.description: Freshwater from melting Antarctic glaciers may be influencing the Southern Ocean in ways scientists have largely overlooked. New research, published in Frontiers in Marine Science, has found that glacial meltwater is not confined to the ocean's surface, as previously assumed, but can also be detected much deeper in coastal waters along the Western Antarctic Peninsula.

phys-org.title: From exporting spyware to surveilling activists—how democracies became the new digital authoritarians
phys-org.description: "Digital authoritarianism" refers to governments using technology for surveillance and censorship to repress dissent. China remains the master practitioner. There, sweeping surveillance and censorship at home is combined with cyber-espionage and disinformation, censorship and influence campaigns abroad.

phys-org.title: People are using AI to communicate without disclosing it. Is this morally wrong?
phys-org.description: Imagine you have used a generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool such as ChatGPT to tidy up notes you took while in a meeting. Your colleague comments on how clear they are. You don't disclose it was the AI that made the notes clear and not you.

phys-org.title: Enduring hardship reduces support for easing hardship for others, study suggests
phys-org.description: Although intuition suggests that experiencing adversity will increase a person's willingness to help others going through similar hardships, surveys show that this is not always the case. For example, immigrants who struggled through arduous naturalization processes do not necessarily support making the path to citizenship easier for others, and those who escaped poverty through hard work often oppose redistributive policies.

phys-org.title: Preparing future math teachers to teach data science
phys-org.description: When Eric Weber, professor and chair of mathematics at Iowa State University, talks about data science with future math teachers, he doesn't begin with code, algorithms, or buzzwords. Instead, he asks them to imagine the scientific method—form a hypothesis, collect data, conduct experiments—running in reverse.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.
